newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Valepar consortium registers for Brazil CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Valepar consortium registers for Brazil CVRD sale.

text.p: The Valepar consortium, one of two consortia due to bid in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD, has registered with the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange to qualify for the sell-off.

Benjamin Steinbruch, chairman of Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN which is leading the Brasil consortium, said the necessary documentation was being delivered to the clearing house of the Rio stock exchange to qualify for the sell-off.

Valepar was the second consortium to register with the bourse by the twice-extended 1930 local time/2230 GMT deadline to qualify for the April 29 auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD at a base price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
In order to qualify the consortia had to present a list of their member companies as well as financial guarantees amounting to 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) among other documents.
Steinbruch said Valepar's constituting companies would be limited to a maximum 20-25 percent stake each in the special purpose company which would administer the CVRD voting stake after the auction.
"Our intention has always been that there would be power sharing, that there would be professional management and that no one would have a majority in this consortium on their own," Steinbruch said.
"Given the importance CVRD represents for Brazil...we thought that the capital (of Valepar) had to be predominantly Brazilian," he added.

Steinbruch said if it won the auction Valepar would create a fund "Fundo Brasil" post privatization that would allow ordinary Brazilians and small and medium sized companies to gain a stake in the special purpose company.
Around 10 percent of the 40-45-percent CVRD voting stake held by Valepar would be set aside to back the fund's stock.

Apart from CSN, Valepar includes Brazilian paper and pulp firm Cia. Suzano, U.S. aluminium company Alcoa, Nations Bank, four Brazilian pension funds and Opportunity Asset Management, an offshore investment fund.

Brazil's largest retail bank Bradesco, which is barred from participating in any consortium bidding for CVRD because it was one of the consultants on the sell-off, will act as a financing agent to one or more of Valepar's members, Steinbruch said.
He said Nations Bank was acting as a financing agent for CSN's stake in the consortium with $1.2 billion as well as being a full member of the consortium.

The four pension funds, which already have a joint voting stake in CVRD of 10.03 percent, are Previ, Petros, Funcef and Funcesp. If CSN wins the auction their stake will give Valepar a controling position in CVRD.

Steinbruch said South African mining firm Gencor might still join the consortium, given that another four to five companies, which could not be named, had been registered with the stock exchange in case they decided to join in the last minute.

The other consortium in the running for CVRD is Valecom, which is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp and which also has a strong Japanese presence.
